summary:
Brazil's national framework applies in Santa Catarina: same-sex marriage has been legal nationwide since 2013 under National Council of Justice Resolution 175/2013, the Supreme Federal Tribunal's 2019 ruling in ADO 26 makes discrimination and hate crimes on sexual-orientation and gender-identity grounds punishable as equivalent to racism under Law 7.716/1989, and gender-marker changes proceed without surgery. A trans visitor's entry, documents and family status are therefore handled on the same footing as any other traveller's.

Santa Catarina's own constitution carries an anti-discrimination clause dating to 2002 that lists sexual orientation among the protected grounds, but as of 2019 it did not address discrimination against transgender people. The constitutional and federal provisions above bind throughout the state and cover that gap in practice.

Documents recording non-binary gender have been obtained in Santa Catarina through the courts or notarial offices since 2020, although no specific law prescribes the practice. The Superior Court of Justice has separately ruled that non-binary people may amend their civil registry to reflect their gender identity.

Florianópolis hosts both a protective judiciary and an established legal infrastructure. Judge M. C. F. Ribeiro da Silva of the 1st Civil Court in Florianópolis blocked immigration authorities from deporting an Italian citizen who had lived more than ten years in a stable relationship with a lesbian Brazilian. A legal guide updated 5 April 2026 names Florianópolis among Brazil's broadly welcoming major cities, with active LGBTQ+ communities, pride events and legal practice accustomed to processing same-sex marriages, adoptions and name or gender-marker changes.

Smaller cities and rural areas of Santa Catarina may present more social friction than the capital, though legal rights are identical nationwide. Foreign same-sex spouses and partners are treated identically for visa and residence categories, including the spousal residence permit, and foreign same-sex marriages are recognised for immigration purposes. Joint and second-parent adoption is settled by the Supreme Federal Tribunal's 2015 ruling in RE 846.102.

Hostility sits at the legislative level rather than in Santa Catarina's own statutes. A deeply conservative Congress has produced a surge of anti-LGBTIQ proposals, including efforts to repeal the marriage equality recogniseded by the Supreme Court in 2013, while the guarantees themselves remain in force. In September 2025 the government reinstated the National LGBTI+ Health Technical Committee, a participatory mechanism dissolved in 2019, for shaping and monitoring inclusive public-health policy.
tangentialFactors:
Santa Catarina's constitutional text is narrower than the national one: the state's 2002 non-discrimination clause names sexual orientation and, as of 2019, did not name gender identity, whereas the Supreme Federal Tribunal's 2019 ruling covers both grounds across the country.

The Florianópolis deportation block is a single-instance judicial decision extending family-based protection to a foreign partner. The sources do not describe it as a rule governing partner deportation in general.

Legislative turbulence is national rather than specific to Santa Catarina: Congress has generated a surge of anti-LGBTIQ proposals, including efforts to repeal the 2013 marriage equality, and the inventory records the proposals without stating their status or outcome.

A legal guide's ranking of Florianópolis as broadly welcoming rests on its own editorial framing; the same guide states that legal rights are identical nationwide, so city-level reputation is a social indicator rather than a difference in entitlement.
localsOnly:
Santa Catarina residents have obtained documents recording non-binary gender through the courts and notarial offices since 2020, a route resting on judicial and notarial practice rather than on any state statute that prescribes it.

The Superior Court of Justice has held that non-binary people may amend their civil registry to reflect their gender identity, giving registry change a national judicial basis independent of state law.

Residents have a participatory channel into inclusive public-health policy through the National LGBTI+ Health Technical Committee, reinstated in September 2025 after its dissolution in 2019 to shape and monitor that policy.

The state constitution's non-discrimination clause, in force since 2002, is the operative state-level text for residents; it names sexual orientation and, as of 2019, did not name gender identity.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Santa Catarina-specific figures on violence against trans people, prosecutions under the 2019 ruling, or police handling of complaints in Florianópolis or elsewhere in the state are carried in this inventory. Enforcement of the protective provisions in practice within Santa Catarina is unresolved here.

Whether Santa Catarina has amended its constitution to name gender identity since 2019 is unresolved; 2019 is the latest position stated in the sources.

The sources do not state which specific documents carry the non-binary marker obtained through Santa Catarina courts and notaries since 2020, or whether those documents are accepted at border control.

Detention and prison placement for trans people in Santa Catarina is not addressed. National Council of Justice Resolution 348 of 13 October 2020, amended by Resolution 366 of 20 January 2021, governs LGBTI placement nationwide on self-declaration and recorded preference, but no Santa Catarina application or compliance data is documented in this inventory.
